request.system: You are clustering code review findings from one PR. Always respond with valid JSON.
request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIRS:
PAIR 1:
A: The Calendar interface now mandates a credentialId routing parameter that TypeScript lets implementers silently ignore (fewer-parameter implementations are legal), and three of the four implementations in this diff (Lark, Office365, BaseCalendarService) do ignore it, so the boundary cannot enforce the per-credential destination selection it was added to guarantee. The next calendar provider — or any future edit to the non-Google implementations — compiles cleanly while creating events on the wrong calendar, which is the exact bug class shipped in this PR, because the contract's key parameter is unenforceable at the interface.
B: Calendar interface change is only half-applied: createEvent's credentialId param is only used by Google; positional untyped arg risks silent fallback to "primary" creating events on the wrong calendar

PAIR 2:
A: The slug condition was silently inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` — an unrelated behavior change smuggled into a destinationCalendar PR with no acceptance. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false, Organization.create runs without the required unique slug and the insert fails, breaking organization creation entirely; with it true, unverified organizations immediately occupy their slug, bypassing the requestedSlug verification flow the adjacent line (153) still implements.
B: The slug spread condition was inverted from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug } to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}, so the Organization create no longer receives a slug when team billing is disabled. On every deployment with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED false (the default for self-hosted installs), Prisma rejects the create because the required slug argument is missing and organization creation returns a 500; with the flag true the slug is additionally assigned immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug approval gating that the adjacent metadata line implements.

PAIR 3:
A: The slug condition was silently inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` — an unrelated behavior change smuggled into a destinationCalendar PR with no acceptance. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false, Organization.create runs without the required unique slug and the insert fails, breaking organization creation entirely; with it true, unverified organizations immediately occupy their slug, bypassing the requestedSlug verification flow the adjacent line (153) still implements.
B: The spread condition was inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, flipping which billing mode sets slug and which sets metadata.requestedSlug. With team billing disabled (self-hosted default), organization creation no longer sets `slug` at all — organizations are created without a URL slug and existing flows that read org slug break; with billing enabled, slug is now written directly AND requestedSlug in metadata, contradicting the billing flow that previously only recorded requestedSlug pending payment.

PAIR 4:
A: N+1 DB queries and fully sequential event creation in createAllCalendarEvents: per-destination loop issues prisma.credential.findUnique and awaits createEvent serially, scaling latency linearly with host count; same shape duplicated in updateAllCalendarEvents (~lines 493-540)
B: Same N+1 pattern in updateAllCalendarEvents: sequential await of prisma.credential.findUnique per calendar reference serializes the loop head even though updateEvent promises are fired concurrently; batch-fetch credentials up front

a.trigger: future calendar provider or edits to non-Google implementations compile cleanly
a.consequence: boundary cannot enforce per-credential destination selection; events created on wrong calendar (silent wrong-calendar bug class)

b.mechanism: createEvent's credentialId param only used by Google; positional untyped argument risks silent fallback to 'primary'
b.consequence: silent fallback to 'primary' creating events on wrong calendar

A names specific implementations; B does not
pairs.reason: Both concern credentialId being ignored by non-Google implementations causing wrong-calendar creation, but A's mechanism is interface-level unenforceability with future-edit trigger, while B claims a positional/untyped-arg silent fallback to 'primary' as the concrete mechanism; material mechanism and trigger details differ.
